Do the following using the steps provided in their respective sections.
        Steps:
        1. clone the repo git@github.com:zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git
        2. analyse the contents of the repo and create following.
            2.1 create/update dockerfile based on the analysis. 
            2.2 kubernetes yamls based on the analysis.
            2.3 github actions file to build application on pushing to main branch.
        3. add all changed file to git changes 
        4. commit / push to repo

function.name: create_a_docker_file
function.description: This function generates a Dockerfile in the specified directory with basic configuration. The Dockerfile will be tailored to a simple Python application. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Dockerfile will be created. It should be a valid directory path relative to the current working directory.

base_image.description: The base image to use for the Dockerfile, representing the starting point for the build.

maintainer.description: The name of the maintainer or author of the Dockerfile.

expose_port.description: The port number that the container should expose. This is typically the port that the application listens on.

entrypoint.description: The command that will be executed when the Docker container starts.

function.name: create_kubernetes_yaml_file
function.description: Generates a Kubernetes deployment and service YAML file in the specified repository directory. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Kubernetes YAML file will be created. This should be the root directory of the repository.

deployment_name.description: The name of the deployment to be created. This should be a unique identifier for the deployment.

image_name.description: The name of the Docker image to be used in the deployment. Include the image version tag if necessary.

replicas.description: The number of replicated pods desired in the deployment.

port.description: The port number that the container exposes for communication.

service_type.description: The type of Kubernetes service to be created for the deployment.

message.content:
Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑use recipe** that you can drop into your local clone of `git@github.com:zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git`. It covers everything you asked for: | Step | What to do | Where to put it | |------|------------|-----------------| | 1 | Clone the repo | `git clone git@github.com:zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git` | | 2 | Analyse & generate artefacts | – Dockerfile – Kubernetes YAML – GitHub Actions workflow | | 3 | Stage the new/updated files | `git add .` | | 4 | Commit & push | `git commit -m "Add CI/CD & infra files"`
`git push origin main` | --- ## 1️⃣ Clone the repository ```bash git clone git@github.com:zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git cd nodejs-welcome ``` > **Tip:** If you don’t have SSH keys set up, use HTTPS instead: > `git clone https://github.com/zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git` --- ## 2️⃣ Analyse the repo & generate artefacts > **Assumptions** > * The app listens on port **3000** (`app.js` or `server.js`). > * The source lives in the repo root (or in a `src/` folder). > * You want to publish the image to **GitHub Container Registry** (`ghcr.io/zelarhq/nodejs-welcome:latest`). > * The Kubernetes cluster is already configured (e.g., via `kubectl`). ### 2.1 Dockerfile Create a file named `Dockerfile` at the repo root: ```dockerfile # syntax=docker/dockerfile:1 FROM node:18-alpine AS builder # Set working directory WORKDIR /app # Install dependencies COPY package*.json ./ RUN npm ci --only=production # Copy source code COPY . . # Expose the port the app listens on EXPOSE 3000 # Start the app CMD ["node", "app.js"] ``` > **Why this Dockerfile?** > * Uses the lightweight `node:18-alpine` image. > * Installs only production deps (`npm ci --only=production`). > * Keeps the image small and reproducible. ### 2.2 Kubernetes YAML Create a file `k8s/deployment.yaml` (you can keep it in a `k8s/` sub‑folder): ```yaml apiVersion: apps/v1 kind: Deployment metadata: name: nodejs-welcome spec: replicas: 2 selector: matchLabels: app: nodejs-welcome template: metadata: labels: app: nodejs-welcome spec: containers: - name: nodejs-welcome image: ghcr.io/zelarhq/nodejs-welcome:latest ports: - containerPort: 3000 env: - name: NODE_ENV value: production --- apiVersion: v1 kind: Service metadata: name: nodejs-welcome spec: selector: app: nodejs-welcome ports: - protocol: TCP port: 80 targetPort: 3000 type: ClusterIP ``` > **What this does** > * Deploys 2 replicas of the container. > * Exposes the app on port 80 inside the cluster (targets 3000). > * Uses `ClusterIP` – change to `NodePort` or `LoadBalancer` if you need external access. ### 2.3 GitHub Actions Workflow Create a file `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: ```yaml name: CI / CD on: push: branches: - main jobs: build-and-push: runs-on: ubuntu-latest permissions: contents: read packages: write # Needed for GHCR steps: - name: Checkout code uses: actions/checkout@v4 - name: Log in to GitHub Container Registry uses: docker/login-action@v3 with: registry: ghcr.io username: ${{ github.actor }} password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }} - name: Set up Docker Buildx uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3 - name: Cache Docker layers uses: actions/cache@v3 with: path: /tmp/.buildx-cache key: ${{ runner.os }}-buildx-${{ github.sha }} restore-keys: | ${{ runner.os }}-buildx- - name: Build and push Docker image uses: docker/build-push-action@v5 with: context: . push: true tags: ghcr.io/zelarhq/nodejs-welcome:latest - name: Verify image run: | docker pull ghcr.io/zelarhq/nodejs-welcome:latest docker run --rm ghcr.io/zelarhq/nodejs-welcome:latest node -v ``` > **Key points** > * Uses the built‑in `GITHUB_TOKEN` for authentication – no extra secrets needed. > * Builds the image on every push to `main` and pushes it to GHCR. > * Caches Docker layers to speed up subsequent builds. --- ## 3️⃣ Stage the new files ```bash git add Dockerfile k8s/deployment.yaml .github/workflows/ci.yml ``` If you prefer to stage everything: ```bash git add . ``` --- ## 4️⃣ Commit & push ```bash git commit -m "Add Dockerfile, K8s manifests, and CI workflow" git push origin main ``` > **After pushing** > * GitHub Actions will automatically trigger the workflow. > * Once the image is pushed to GHCR, you can deploy it to your cluster: ```bash kubectl apply -f k8s/deployment.yaml ``` --- ### 🎉 Done! You now have: * A production‑ready Docker image. * Kubernetes manifests for deployment & service. * A fully automated CI pipeline that builds & publishes the image on every push to `main`. Feel free to tweak the image tag, replica count, or service type to suit your environment. Happy coding!
